content: The University of Edinburgh, located in the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, collaborated with external experts and WHO staff in the preparation of recommendations. Among the contributors were: Hoang Thi Tran, a neonatologist and Deputy Director of Da Nang Hospital for Women and Children in Vietnam. She also serves as the Acting Head of the Department of Paediatrics at the School of Medicine and Pharmacy, University of Da Nang. Khalid Yunis, a Professor of Pediatrics and Head of the Division of Neonatology at the Department of Pediatrics and Adolescent Medicine, American University of Beirut Medical Center, Lebanon. Partner Organizations and Observers included: Deborah Armbruster, Senior Maternal and Newborn Health Advisor at USAID’s Bureau for Global Health, United States. Hilary Gammill, Deputy Director of Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health Discovery and Tools at the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, United States. Leah Greenspan, from USAID’s Bureau for Global Health, Washington, United States. William Keenan, Executive Director of the International Pediatric Association, United States. Andrew Shennan, Chair of the FIGO Committee and Professor of Obstetrics at King’s College London, United Kingdom. Ingela Wiklund, Associate Professor and Board Member at the Karolinska Institute, Sweden, and Head of the Institution for Health and Welfare. The Evidence Synthesis Group (ESG) included: Jenny Cao, Research Officer in the Maternal, Child, and Adolescent Health Program at the Burnet Institute, Australia. Leanne Jones, Deputy Managing Editor of Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth, Department of Women’s and Children’s Health, University of Liverpool, United Kingdom. Frances Kellie, Managing Editor of Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth, University of Liverpool, and Liverpool Women’s NHS Foundation Trust, United Kingdom. Victoria Hodgetts-Morton, Research Fellow at the University of Birmingham, United Kingdom. Katie Morris, Director of the Birmingham Clinical Trials Unit, University of Birmingham, United Kingdom. Jen Ramson, Guideline Methodologist in the Maternal, Child, and Adolescent Health Program at the Burnet Institute, Australia. Joshua Vogel, Co-Head of the Global Women’s and Newborn’s Health Group at the Burnet Institute, Australia. Myfanwy Williams, Research Associate and Guideline Methodologist at Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth, University of Liverpool, United Kingdom. The WHO Recommendation on Tocolytic Therapy for Improving Preterm Birth Outcomes was supported by systematic review team leaders: Meghan Bohren, Associate Professor of Gender and Women’s Health at the Centre for Health Equity, University of Melbourne, Australia. Ioannis Gallos, Clinician and Scientist at Tommy’s National Centre for Miscarriage Research, University of Birmingham, United Kingdom. WHO Country and Regional Offices involved: Bremen De Mucio, Advisor on Sexual and Reproductive Health. Adrian Pablo Duran, Advisor on Perinatal Health. Karima Gholbzouri, Regional Advisor. Chandani Anoma Jayathilaka, Medical Officer. Oleg Kuzmenko, Technical Officer for Reproductive Health. Nancy Kidula, Medical Officer for Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health. Priya Mannava, Technical Officer for Health Information. Neena Raina, Coordinator. Howard Sobel, Regional Advisor. The WHO Steering Group included members from the Department of Sexual and Reproductive Health and Research (SRH): Olufemi Oladapo, Unit Head of the Maternal and Perinatal Health Unit. Doris Chou, Medical Officer for Maternal and Perinatal Health. Tina Lavin, Technical Officer for Maternal and Perinatal Health. Maurice Bucagu, Medical Officer for the Maternal Health Unit. Rajiv Bahl, Unit Head of the Newborn Health Unit. Ayesha De Costa, Scientist in the Newborn Health Unit. Karen Edmond, Scientist in the Newborn Health Unit. The External Review Group included: Edgardo Abalos, Head of the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology and Vice Director of Centro Rosarino de Estudios Perinatales, Rosario, Argentina. Philippa Middleton, Associate Professor of Perinatal Epidemiology at the South Australian Health and Medical Research Institute, Adelaide, Australia. Suneeta Mittal, Professor of Obstetrics and Gynaecology at Fortis Memorial Research Institute, Gurugram, India. Siddarth Ramji, Professor of Neonatology at Maulana Azad Medical College, New Delhi, India. Haroon Saloojee, Professor of Pediatrics in the Division of Community Pediatrics, University of the Witwatersrand, Johannesburg, South Africa. The recommendations prioritized outcomes such as maternal well-being, maternal satisfaction, and adverse effects of treatment (e.g., chorioamnionitis, puerperal sepsis, postnatal fever). Neonatal outcomes included conditions such as cerebral palsy, developmental delays, and sensory impairments (e.g., hearing or visual impairments).
